key_insight: Free-energy predictions for disordered alloys can be systematically improved by expanding in energy cumulants, capturing short-range order beyond the usual special quasirandom structure + ideal entropy approximation.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening of disordered materials and phase stability without costly Monte Carlo or molecular dynamics, helping identify synthesizable compositions and finite-temperature order–disorder behavior.
method: Treat the conventional SQS+ideal entropy estimate as the first term in an infinite cumulant expansion of the free energy.
Estimate higher-order energy cumulants directly from energies of random atomic arrangements.
Apply the framework to predict phase diagrams, defect concentrations, and short-range order in complex alloys and Li-excess rocksalt oxides.
evidence_signal: In a nine-element refractory system, including the second cumulant reduced free-energy errors by about an order of magnitude, and the approach was used to screen Li-excess rocksalt oxides across 26 elements.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on how well random-arrangement energy samples capture the relevant cumulants, so sparse sampling or strong local correlations may limit reliability.
paper_title: Beyond special quasirandom structures: free energies from energy cumulants
